scope: Claim-level trichome development, gland-class, secretory-cell ultrastructure, sampling, and cannabinoid precursor evidence for THC-ENC-221 through THC-ENC-227.
rules: Morphology, gland class, secretion, tissue chemistry, and whole-flower chemistry remain distinct measurements.
Microscopy and isolated-trichome chemistry support localization and class-specific observations but do not directly quantify whole-crop cannabinoid yield.
Pathway localization and biochemical precursor evidence do not establish universal cultivation interventions or rate-limiting steps.
All mappings remain pending independent science review.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis capitate trichomes develop asynchronously and show genotype- and plant-age-dependent differences in abundance, stalk formation, head morphology, senescence, dehiscence, and drying-related morphology.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Punja, Sutton, and Kim 2023 abstract, methods, results, and conclusion.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports developmental staging of glandular trichomes and caution against one visual maturity rule.
claimEvidence.limitations: The study examined a limited genotype set and organ context; observed stage boundaries are method- and tissue-dependent.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Bulbous glandular trichomes are an anatomically recognized cannabis trichome class, but their small size and relative contribution to whole-flower cannabinoid production should not be inferred from class identity alone.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Punja, Sutton, and Kim 2023 morphology/classification observations.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports anatomical recognition of bulbous trichomes and method-aware classification.
claimEvidence.limitations: The source does not establish a universal quantitative contribution of bulbous glands to whole-flower cannabinoid yield.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Capitate-sessile trichomes are directly observed on cannabis reproductive tissues, can predominate earlier in flower development, and contain measurable cannabinoids in isolated-trichome analyses.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Punja, Sutton, and Kim 2023 developmental morphology; Happyana et al. 2013 SEM/LMD-LCMS analysis.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports class identification, developmental context, and the distinction between morphology and direct chemical measurement.
claimEvidence.limitations: Not every sessile-appearing gland necessarily follows the same developmental trajectory, and isolated-gland chemistry does not quantify whole-flower contribution.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Capitate-stalked cannabis trichomes show measurable developmental changes and contain cannabinoid-rich secretory tissue, while ultrastructural work localizes major pathway machinery to specialized secretory-cell compartments.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Punja, Sutton, and Kim 2023 stalk/head development; Happyana et al. 2013 isolated capitate-stalked chemistry; Livingston et al. 2022 ultrastructure/pathway localization.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports capitate-stalked morphology and their central role in specialized-metabolite production.
claimEvidence.limitations: Trichome morphology alone does not establish whole-tissue chemistry or per-gland production rate.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis glandular trichome secretory cells form a polarized multicellular system with specialized organelle organization and extracellular-facing THCAS localization adjacent to the storage cavity.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Livingston et al. 2022 highlights, summary, and electron-microscopy/immunolocalization results.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports secretory-disk cell organization, extracellular cavity context, and compartment-aware pathway diagrams.
claimEvidence.limitations: Some intracellular trafficking steps remain proposed rather than directly observed; diagrams should separate localization evidence from pathway-transport hypotheses.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis trichome abundance and morphology vary with genotype, plant age, surface, and developmental position, so trichome-density comparisons require an explicit tissue, surface, developmental stage, imaging method, and denominator.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Punja, Sutton, and Kim 2023 surface/genotype/age counts; Happyana et al. 2013 SEM distribution/density observations.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports repeatable sampling frames and explicit denominators for trichome-density claims.
claimEvidence.limitations: Density is only one component of chemical production and cannot substitute for matched tissue chemistry.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Hexanoyl-CoA is directly detected in cannabis tissues associated with cannabinoid biosynthesis, and trichome-localized evidence supports specialized compartmentation of cannabinoid/terpene precursor metabolism.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Stout et al. 2012 LC-MS/MS, CsAAE1 expression/activity, and localization results; Livingston et al. 2022 pathway-localization results.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports hexanoyl-CoA and isoprenoid precursor context in trichome cannabinoid biosynthesis.
claimEvidence.limitations: The upstream origin of hexanoate and quantitative control of intact-plant pathway flux remain incompletely resolved; precursor presence does not imply a cultivation prescription.
